title: Interactive continental explorer defaults
interpretation: Population values are coarse regional teaching presets. Migration, mixing, Tasmania population, and barrier/contact values are explicitly separated into empirical constraints versus sensitivity assumptions.

population_preset_9000_bce.status: secondary-source regional reconstruction; values rounded to people

aggregation_notes.Asia: Asia 1,317,000 + CIS 238,000 in the source table
aggregation_notes.Americas: Latin America 363,000 + North America 52,000 in the source table
aggregation_notes.Australia/Oceania: Source-table Oceania total minus the separate Tasmania teaching placeholder.
aggregation_notes.Tasmania: 7,465 is NOT a 9000 BCE estimate. It is a teaching placeholder taken from the middle published early-contact population model in Model 10 because the repository does not contain a defensible Tasmania-specific 11 ka population estimate.

source.label: Statista historical continental population table, 9000 BCE row
source.note: Used because the table provides a separate Middle East category. Prehistoric values are highly uncertain.

population_target_2000_ce.status: same source-compatible endpoint; used only to create a smooth visual population trajectory

aggregation_notes.Australia/Oceania: Teaching endpoint after separating Tasmania from the source-table Oceania total.
aggregation_notes.Tasmania: Approximate whole-island modern population scale used only for visualization; not an Indigenous-population reconstruction.

global_crosscheck.finding: Global population estimate for 10,000 BCE about 4.4 million, with very wide uncertainty (<0.01 to 8.9 million in the paper's scenario range).

parent_source_offdiag_default.status: modeler-chosen teaching sensitivity preset; NOT an empirical Holocene migration matrix
parent_source_offdiag_default.semantics: row=destination child's region, column=source region; value=fraction of parental draws from that external region per generation

mixing_strength_default.status: modeler-chosen sensitivity parameter; 0=no descendant-status diffusion beyond pooled composition, 1=full random mating within macroregion

late_contact_default.status: teaching sensitivity control, not an empirical global contact estimate

population_anchors_bce.status: secondary-source regional reconstruction used for date-responsive teaching presets; values are people
population_anchors_bce.interpolation: Notebook log-interpolates source-table continental anchors. Tasmania is held at the explicit 7,465 teaching placeholder across prehistoric anchors because a defensible 11 ka Tasmania population estimate is not encoded.

source.label: Statista historical continental population table, 9000 BCE row
source.note: Used because the table provides a separate Middle East category. Prehistoric values are highly uncertain.

tasmania_barrier_default.status: The hard barrier before recent contact is an evidence-constrained structural assumption. The 229-year release uses 1797-to-2026 as the earliest sustained-contact sensitivity marker. The post-release parent-source rate remains a teaching parameter, not an empirical estimate.

stochastic_default.status: Pedigree Monte Carlo conditional on the selected demographic/migration parameters. It is not parameter uncertainty and not a posterior probability of the historical scenario.
